summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, morbid obesity, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for hypotension and presyncope following excessive diuretic use and dehydration. He had recently increased his torsemide dose, leading to volume depletion, acute kidney injury, and electrolyte imbalances. Evaluation ruled out adrenal insufficiency, heart failure, and pulmonary embolism. Treatment included IV fluids, adjustment of antihypertensives, initiation of spironolactone, reduction of dexamethasone to 1 mg daily, and fluid restriction. His renal function normalized, blood pressure stabilized, and edema improved. He was discharged home with instructions to monitor fluid intake, adjust carvedilol based on blood pressure, and follow up on labs.
